capabilities: capture memos on a tile board stored as .codex files
run AI persona annotations in single, parallel, or sequential debate modes
draw five-card idea packs with grade levels, difficulty, and cross-seed synthesis
generate synthesis insights bridging card categories and promote cards to markdown notes
connect via subscription plans through Claude Code and Antigravity CLIs or BYOK API keys
disambiguation: Not a coding tool despite the name and .codex files; those are just its own JSON workbench file format for card data.
extras: The Korean documentation is stated to be the canonical version, with a shorter English About section. The plugin does not work without AI integration. The README warns that older versions stored plan tokens in plaintext and that Dropbox-synced vaults can cache stale plugin builds after updates; BRAT is supported for beta installs.
intentEvidence: 원래의 mskayyali/Notepad 앱이 너무 강력해서 옵시디언 플러그인으로 옮겼고
motivation: The author ported the standalone mskayyali/Notepad app into Obsidian because it was powerful, adding a metacognitive difficulty-based card-drawing system and MikaNote-style visuals.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in board for dumping memos and getting AI personas to debate and annotate them, nor a way to force new thinking angles when writing stalls.
